evidence.description: First symptom: water-soaked lesions on the fruit surface near the calyx; infected nuts lose their lustre.
evidence.quote: The first visible symptom is the appearance of water soaked lesions on the surface of fruits near the calyx. The infected nuts lose their lustre.
evidence.source: Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod — Extension Folder No. 17: Koleroga (Mahali) of arecanut (1989-08), p. 2

evidence.description: The disease is seasonal, during the South-West monsoon, and is reported from Kerala, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
evidence.quote: The disease is seasonal and occurs during the South-West monsoon period in Kerala, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
evidence.source: Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod — Extension Folder No. 17: Koleroga (Mahali) of arecanut (1989-08), p. 2

management: Collect infected and fallen fruits regularly and destroy them to reduce the source of infection and further spread.

evidence.description: ICAR-CPCRI: before monsoon onset in endemic areas, spray 1% Bordeaux mixture, once more after 45 days, and again if the rains are prolonged.
evidence.quote: It is important to adopt prophylactic treatment in disease endemic areas before the onset of monsoon by spraying 1% Bordeaux mixture and one more spray after 45 days. If the rainy period is extended, one more spray is also required.
evidence.source: ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (ICAR-CPCRI), Kasaragod — Crop protection: integrated management of pests and diseases for the successful cultivation of coconut, arecanut and cocoa (2022-11/12), p. 2

evidence.description: CPCRI folder (arecanut Koleroga): 1% Bordeaux mixture prophylactic spraying; two sprays (after pre-monsoon showers and 40-45 days later), a third if the monsoon prolongs.
evidence.quote: Prophylactic spraying with 1 % Bordeaux mixture gives satisfactory control of the disease. Two sprayings are generally required, first after the premonsoon showers and the second 40-45 days thereafter. If the monsoon prolongs, a third spraying will be required.
evidence.source: Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod — Extension Folder No. 17: Koleroga (Mahali) of arecanut (1989-08), p. 2

evidence.description: Spraying 0.5% mandipropamid 23.4% SC was found equally effective in managing arecanut fruit rot in endemic areas.
evidence.quote: Spraying of 0.5% mandipropamid 23.4% SC, a contact and translaminar fungicide was found equally effective in managing the fruit rot of arecanut in disease endemic areas.
evidence.source: ICAR-Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (ICAR-CPCRI), Kasaragod — Crop protection: integrated management of pests and diseases for the successful cultivation of coconut, arecanut and cocoa (2022-11/12), p. 2
